clue.text: Psychiatrist unusually given toil by hesitant character

parts.note: shrink is slang for a psychiatrist (headshrinker)

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of the following words appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist is oddly handed hard work by a timid patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Psychiatrist' leads toward a medical clue, but it only supplies slang; 'unusually' signals the rearrangement, giving INGVIOLET.
explanation.definitionFit: A shy, retiring person who hangs back is proverbially called by this flower-based idiom.

clue.text: 13 shops around looking for takers

parts.note: 13 is EYE, slang for a detective (private eye); these eyes go round department stores watching for shoplifters, the 'takers'

explanation.surface: Something wanders round the shops hunting for people who will accept an offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takers' sounds like willing customers but means thieves who take goods without paying.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain-clothes staff employed by a shop to watch for and catch shoplifters.

clue.text: No old Ford vehicles assembled in Rugby

indicators.note: No tells us to go without the letter that the old car supplies

parts.note: trucks are goods vehicles
the Model T was Ford's famous early car, so T

explanation.surface: No vintage Ford vehicles were put together in the town of Rugby.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby looks like the Warwickshire town, but it is the sport; the Model T is the classic early Ford.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union, players bind together over a loose ball in a formation of this name.

clue.text: Directions to Leeds, perhaps with 13s

parts.note: N and E, north and east, two compass directions

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the city's name might be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Instructions on getting to the city of Leeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 refers to the answer at 13-across, EYE: each sewing needle has one. 'perhaps' rearranges the city name to give EDLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewing implements each have an eye, the hole the thread passes through.

clue.text: Chanted wrong note — din resulted

indicators.note: a wrong note is one out of place, so the letters of note and din are disordered

explanation.surface: A singer hit a bad note and a racket followed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' shuffles NOTE and DIN; 'resulted' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To intone is to recite in a chanting, monotonous voice, as in church.

clue.text: Force cut as swept with 13

parts.note: G is the symbol for the force of gravity, as in g-force
lanced means cut open, as a boil

explanation.surface: A forceful cricket stroke was played as the batsman swept.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is EYE: to glance is to sweep the eye quickly over something.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking briefly and quickly at something means passing one's gaze over it.

clue.text: Things are left to you to do it

definitions.text: Things are left to you to do it

parts.words: Things are left to you to do it
parts.note: things left to you in a will are what you receive as an heir

explanation.surface: Tasks are left for you to handle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left to you' suggests responsibility but means bequeathed.
explanation.definitionFit: Receiving property bequeathed by someone who has died is the act described.

clue.text: "What's yours?", perhaps

parts.note: a friend at the pub, a British '... out an offer to buy the next drink

explanation.surface: A host asks what drink you would like.
explanation.walkthrough: A LOCAL is a British neighbourhood pub; the phrase also means a nearby phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephone call to a nearby number, reread as a shout heard in one's pub.

clue.text: Consider how to foster interest

definitions.meaning: to weigh up or allow for
putting money into a bank account so that it earns interest

explanation.definitionFit: To factor something in is to consider it; money placed in a bank earns interest.

clue.text: Players reported to be banned?

parts.note: musical players form a band, a word said the same as banned

explanation.surface: Sportsmen are rumoured to have been suspended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' and 'banned' suggest sport and discipline; the pun is band.
explanation.definitionFit: A large group of instrumental musicians playing together is a kind of band.

clue.text: Heart honours may modify a letter …

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games
the ace is an honour card in bridge
K, the king, is another honour card

explanation.surface: Winning cards in the heart suit can change a correspondent's letter.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge honours are ace, king, queen, jack and ten.
explanation.definitionFit: A diacritic mark, the small inverted circumflex, alters a letter's sound in Czech.

clue.text: … letter spoiled by one slip

indicators.note: spoiled means ruined, so the letters of one and slip are jumbled

explanation.surface: A letter was ruined by a single blot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoiled' rearranges ONE and SLIP.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifth character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Musician turns sick at heart

parts.note: the core is the heart of something

indicators.note: turns says the word for sick is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: ill means sick

explanation.surface: A musician becomes nauseous deep down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses the word for sick, giving LLI; 'at' is just a link. The surface suggests nausea, but the musician is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcangelo Corelli was an Italian Baroque violinist and composer.

clue.text: The Observer, entered as Paper of the Year

indicators.note: entered as says the letters are found inside the following words

explanation.surface: The Observer newspaper was named Paper of the Year.
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer looks like the newspaper but means a watcher; the run sits across 'the Year'.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ that observes, the part of the body that sees.

clue.text: Showed speedo times to be erratic

indicators.note: erratic means wandering irregularly, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign

explanation.surface: A speedometer's readings proved unreliable.
explanation.walkthrough: SPEEDO plus X is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal or display something is to lay it open to view.

clue.text: Capital curtailed entry document for all equably

indicators.note: curtailed means having its tail cut off, losing its last letter

parts.note: Paris is the capital of France
a pass is a permit to enter
U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all

explanation.surface: A capital city shortened its entry paperwork for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' removes S from PARIS; U is the universal film rating in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin phrase meaning side by side, at equal pace, on an equal footing.

clue.text: Stick had mysteriously gone before

indicators.note: mysteriously gone says the letters of had vanish from the longer word, though not in the order the clue prints them

parts.note: adhere means stick
the three letters of had, taken in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: A stick that someone owned vanished earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of HAD, rearranged as ADH, are removed from ADHERE.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic or poetic word meaning earlier than.

clue.text: Diminish time hauled back

indicators.note: back says the whole run is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: carted means hauled

explanation.surface: Time was dragged backwards and reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses TCARTED.
explanation.definitionFit: To take away from or lessen something's worth.

clue.text: Age of girl not five

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the numeral's letter

parts.note: Vera is a girl's name
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A girl's age is not five.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes V from VERA.
explanation.definitionFit: A period of history is an epoch or age.

clue.text: Rogue seen about to steal dresses

indicators.note: about says one piece goes round the other
rogue as an adjective means behaving wildly, so the letters of seen run astray

parts.note: rob means steal

explanation.surface: A rogue was seen about to steal some dresses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rogue' turns SEEN into ENES, and 'about' wraps it round the theft word. The surface makes 'dresses' sound like stolen clothes; here it is a verb meaning clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To robe someone formally is to clothe them.

clue.text: Courageous display, which gives lift against difficulty

parts.note: a bra gives uplift
V is short for versus, against
ado means fuss or difficulty

explanation.surface: Showing courage, which raises one's spirits in hard times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lift' sounds like spirits but is the uplift of a bra.
explanation.definitionFit: A show of boldness meant to impress, often with little behind it.

clue.text: Thus somehow toils a lone performer

parts.note: so means thus

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of toils are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: So a solitary performer works hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' makes LOIST from TOILS.
explanation.definitionFit: A musician performing alone, without accompaniment or ensemble.

clue.text: Top girl star

parts.note: a cap is a top or lid
Ella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: The top girl is a star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'star' looks like praise for the girl but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The brightest star in the constellation Auriga.

clue.text: Fellow that's after appointment with the church

indicators.note: after places the that-is letters behind the appointment

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
app is a short form of appointment
IE, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A man who is chasing a date with the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the Latin 'that is' behind the short form of appointment, with the church abbreviation at the front. APP for appointment is informal.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned British colloquial word for a man or fellow.

clue.text: Photo with some colour in high wind

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a photo

indicators.note: some means only part of the colour word is kept, its final two letters dropped

explanation.surface: A photograph with a little colour in a strong gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' drops UR from colour to leave COLO. 'high wind' suggests a gale but means a high-pitched wind instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The small flute pitched an octave above the standard one.

clue.text: Expression of surprise at topless Winnie

indicators.note: topless says the first letter is removed

parts.note: Winnie-the-Pooh, the bear in A. A. Milne's stories

explanation.surface: A gasp at a bear without his top on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes P from POOH.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of wonder or delight.

clue.text: Oil taps failed, given wind force at sea

indicators.note: failed means broke down, so the letters of oil taps come out jumbled

explanation.surface: Oil taps broke down despite a strong wind at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failed' rearranges OIL TAPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sail set above the lowest on a mast, filled by the wind on a ship.

clue.text: Austere character like vinegar hiding a saint

indicators.note: hiding says the saint's letter is concealed inside

parts.note: acetic means of or like vinegar

explanation.surface: An austere sour person conceals a holy figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding' puts S inside ACETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A person practising severe self-denial for religious reasons.

clue.text: Bring up Fido, say, with ease, say, in Sioux dwelling

indicators.note: bring up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Fido is a typical dog's name, so a pet

indicators.note: say signals the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: ease is said like E's, two letter Es

explanation.surface: Raise your dog in comfort in a Native American home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring up' turns PET to TEP; 'say' makes ease sound like two Es.
explanation.definitionFit: A conical tent of the Plains peoples of North America.

clue.text: Sackville-West keeps son in view

indicators.note: keeps says one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: Vita Sackville-West, the English writer and gardener

explanation.surface: Vita Sackville-West keeps her son in sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' puts S into VITA.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasant outlook or prospect seen at a distance.

clue.text: I am ready to turn on the 30 …

parts.note: I'm is short for I am
prompt means ready, quick
U as in a U-turn

explanation.surface: I'm prepared to turn on the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 30 is SPUR-OF-THE-MOMENT, so the definition means improvised.
explanation.definitionFit: Done without preparation, improvised there and then.

clue.text: … whereon politicians set policies, perhaps, for men put them so?

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the words that follow could be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Politicians make policy on a whim, and for what reason?
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges FOR MEN PUT THEM SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Policies set on impulse are made without forethought, in a sudden moment.
